cat > programs/task-870789c9.py <<'PY'
def transform(grid):
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # Find monochrome connected components; hollow rectangular frames are filled with 2.
    seen = set()
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            color = grid[r][c]
            if color in (0, 5, 9) or (r, c) in seen:
                continue
            stack = [(r, c)]
            seen.add((r, c))
            comp = set()
            while stack:
                y, x = stack.pop()
                comp.add((y, x))
                for dy, dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    p = (y+dy, x+dx)
                    if 0 <= p[0] < h and 0 <= p[1] < w and p not in seen and grid[p[0]][p[1]] == color:
                        seen.add(p)
                        stack.append(p)
            r0, r1 = min(y for y,x in comp), max(y for y,x in comp)
            c0, c1 = min(x for y,x in comp), max(x for y,x in comp)
            if r1-r0 >= 2 and c1-c0 >= 2:
                border = {(y,x) for y in range(r0,r1+1) for x in range(c0,c1+1)
                          if y in (r0,r1) or x in (c0,c1)}
                if comp == border:
                    for y in range(r0+1,r1):
                        for x in range(c0+1,c1):
                            out[y][x] = 2
    # Change the center cell of an 8-cell 3x3 ring of 6 to 7.
    for r in range(h-2):
        for c in range(w-2):
            if all(grid[r+dr][c+dc] == 6
                   for dr in range(3) for dc in range(3) if (dr,dc) != (1,1)):
                out[r+1][c+1] = 7
    return out
PY

def transform(grid):
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    seen = set()
    # Hollow rectangular frames are filled according to the parity of their interior:
    # odd-by-odd interiors become 7; even-by-even interiors become 2.
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            color = grid[r][c]
            if (r, c) in seen:
                continue
            stack = [(r, c)]
            seen.add((r, c))
            comp = set()
            while stack:
                y, x = stack.pop()
                comp.add((y, x))
                for dy, dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    yy, xx = y+dy, x+dx
                    if 0 <= yy < h and 0 <= xx < w and (yy,xx) not in seen and grid[yy][xx] == color:
                        seen.add((yy,xx))
                        stack.append((yy,xx))
            r0, r1 = min(y for y,x in comp), max(y for y,x in comp)
            c0, c1 = min(x for y,x in comp), max(x for y,x in comp)
            if r1-r0 >= 2 and c1-c0 >= 2:
                border = {(y,x) for y in range(r0,r1+1) for x in range(c0,c1+1)
                          if y in (r0,r1) or x in (c0,c1)}
                if comp == border:
                    ih, iw = r1-r0-1, c1-c0-1
                    fill = 7 if ih % 2 == 1 and iw % 2 == 1 else 2
                    for y in range(r0+1,r1):
                        for x in range(c0+1,c1):
                            out[y][x] = fill
    # The center of any 3x3 ring is also marked 7.
    for r in range(h-2):
        for c in range(w-2):
            if all(grid[r+dr][c+dc] != grid[r+1][c+1]
                   for dr in range(3) for dc in range(3) if (dr,dc)!=(1,1)):
                # Ring perimeter is one uniform color and center differs.
                ring = [grid[r+dr][c+dc] for dr in range(3) for dc in range(3) if (dr,dc)!=(1,1)]
                if len(set(ring)) == 1:
                    out[r+1][c+1] = 7
    return out
PY
